Your query **"sonar 2"** likely refers to one of two distinct things: **Perplexity's Sonar AI model family** or **OpenAI's Sora 2 video generation model**. Here's a thorough breakdown of both.

***
## Perplexity Sonar (2025–2026)
Perplexity's **Sonar** is a proprietary family of AI models designed specifically for fast, real-time, search-grounded answers with inline citations. The original Sonar launched on **February 11, 2025**, built on Meta's Llama 3.3 70B architecture, and became the default engine for all free-tier users. It features a 128K context window and is optimized for low-latency web retrieval.[1]
The "new Sonar" — released in **March 2026** — made significant performance leaps. Powered by **Cerebras inference infrastructure**, it runs at roughly **1,200 tokens per second**, making it nearly 10x faster than comparable models like Gemini 2.0 Flash. In user satisfaction evaluations, the new Sonar outperforms both GPT-4o mini and Claude 3.5 Haiku by a substantial margin, and even exceeds Claude 3.5 Sonnet, closely approaching GPT-4o at a fraction of its cost.[2]

Perplexity's **Sonar-Reasoning-Pro** is the most powerful variant in the family and earned a score of **1136** on the Search Arena leaderboard — statistically tied with Gemini 2.5 Pro Grounding at the top position. Notably, Sonar Pro models cite **2–3x more sources** than equivalent Gemini models, reflecting a deeper search architecture.[3]

***
## Sonar Model Variants
The Sonar family is tiered by capability and speed:[4]

| Model | Best For | Key Trait |
|---|---|---|
| **Sonar** | Quick factual queries, topic summaries | Fastest, default for free users |
| **Sonar Pro** | Complex research, detailed answers | More sources, deeper search |
| **Sonar Reasoning Pro** | Multi-step analysis, advanced tasks | Top leaderboard performance |

***
## OpenAI Sora 2
If your query was about **OpenAI's Sora 2**, that is a completely different product — a **video generation model** released in September 2025. Sora 2 represents a major leap in AI video, capable of generating physically accurate, realistic scenes including complex athletic maneuvers like Olympic gymnastics and triple axels, which prior video models could not reproduce.[5]

Technically, Sora 2 uses a **Multimodal Diffusion Transformer (MM-DiT)** architecture that processes text, images, and audio simultaneously. One of its headline features is **native synchronized audio generation** — the model produces dialogue, sound effects, and ambient noise at the same time as the video, rather than as a post-processing step. Videos can run from 10 to 25 seconds in length.[6]

Which of these two — Perplexity's Sonar model family or OpenAI's Sora 2 video generator — were you asking about?
